title: Explicit simple-root relations criterion for a group-scheme homomorphism
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ a pinned split realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], with nonempty base $\Delta$. Use the canonical root groups $U_\gamma$, root exponentials $\exp_\gamma$, linked generators, representatives $n_\alpha$, reflections $s_\alpha$, integers $m_{\alpha\beta}$, elements $t_{\alpha\beta}\in T(A)$, and positive two-root subgroups $U_{\Psi_{\alpha\beta}}$ of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. Let $H$ be an affine $A$-group scheme, meaning an affine scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Give group-scheme homomorphisms $f_T:T\to H$, $f_\alpha:U_\alpha\to H$ and sections $h_\alpha\in H(A)$ for $\alpha\in\Delta$. For every unordered pair of distinct simple roots give a homomorphism $q_{\alpha\beta}:U_{\Psi_{\alpha\beta}}\to H$ restricting to $f_\alpha$ and $f_\beta$. Suppose the following identities hold after every commutative $A$-algebra extension $R$, for all the indicated points:
$$f_T(t)f_\alpha(u)f_T(t)^{-1}=f_\alpha(tut^{-1}),\qquad h_\alpha f_T(t)h_\alpha^{-1}=f_T(s_\alpha(t))\quad(t\in T(R),u\in U_\alpha(R));$$
$$h_\alpha^2=f_T(\alpha^\vee(-1)),\qquad (h_\alpha h_\beta)^{m_{\alpha\beta}}=f_T(t_{\alpha\beta})\quad(\alpha\ne\beta);$$
$$(h_\alpha f_\alpha(\exp_\alpha(X_\alpha)))^3=1;$$
$$h_\alpha q_{\alpha\beta}(u)h_\alpha^{-1}=q_{\alpha\beta}(n_\alpha u n_\alpha^{-1})\quad(u\in U_c(R),\ c\in\Psi_{\alpha\beta}\setminus\{\alpha\});$$
$$h_\beta q_{\alpha\beta}(u)h_\beta^{-1}=q_{\alpha\beta}(n_\beta u n_\beta^{-1})\quad(u\in U_c(R),\ c\in\Psi_{\alpha\beta}\setminus\{\beta\}).$$
Then there is a unique $A$-group-scheme homomorphism $f:G\to H$ with $f|_T=f_T$, $f|_{U_\alpha}=f_\alpha$, and $f(n_\alpha)=h_\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$. More generally, any two homomorphisms $G\to H$ with these same torus restrictions, simple-root restrictions and values on the $n_\alpha$ are equal, without additional assumptions on the supplied data. No Noetherian, connectedness, reducedness or residue-characteristic hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normalizer-torus-weyl-presentation] to $f_T$ and the $h_\alpha$. Its three hypotheses are exactly the torus-reflection, square and pair relations assumed in the item. This gives $f_N:N_G(T)\to H$ with $f_N|_T=f_T$ and $f_N(n_\alpha)=h_\alpha$. The normalizer stage uses no positive-root multiplication assumption.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.4 proof, printed pp.202–203; full-root criterion Theorem 6.2.1, pp.198–200. Agent assembly from the displayed statements; no external proof is imported.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-simple-root-weyl-transport] using this $f_N$, the given $f_\alpha$, and the supplied $q_{\alpha\beta}$. The torus-equivariance, cubic and two rank-two conjugation identities are precisely its hypotheses; the normalizer restrictions identify its $f_T,h_\alpha$ with the given ones. It supplies all-root maps $g_\gamma$, normalizer equivariance, and $F_\alpha$ on each rank-one centralizer. It also supplies $g_c=q_{\alpha\beta}|_{U_c}$ for every $c\in\Psi_{\alpha\beta}$, including the nonsimple roots; knowing this only for simple roots would not suffice.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.4 proof, printed pp.202–203; full-root criterion Theorem 6.2.1, pp.198–200. Agent assembly from the displayed statements; no external proof is imported.

proof.text: In [lem-sfb-full-root-hom-extension], take the $f_N$, $g_\gamma$, $F_\alpha$ from steps 1–2 and the original $q_{\alpha\beta}$. Normalizer equivariance, both opposite-root restrictions of $F_\alpha$, its restriction on $N\cap K_\alpha$, and every root restriction of $q_{\alpha\beta}$ are provided by step 2. Thus that criterion yields $f:G\to H$ extending $f_N$ and every $g_\gamma$. Its torus and simple-root restrictions are $f_T$ and $f_\alpha$, and $f(n_\alpha)=f_N(n_\alpha)=h_\alpha$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.4 proof, printed pp.202–203; full-root criterion Theorem 6.2.1, pp.198–200. Agent assembly from the displayed statements; no external proof is imported.

proof.text: For the unconditional uniqueness clause, let $f,f\prime:G\to H$ have the same given restrictions. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-sfb-normalizer-torus-weyl-presentation] makes their normalizer restrictions equal: its hypotheses hold because applying either homomorphism to the Weyl-calculus identities preserves them. For any root $\gamma$, apply [lem-sfb-simple-root-weyl-transport] to the data obtained by restricting $f$ (with $q_{\alpha\beta}=f|_{U_{\Psi_{\alpha\beta}}}$). Its identities follow by applying $f$ to the root-calculus identities, so it supplies a simple $\beta$ and a word $n$ with $w\beta=\gamma$. For $u\in U_\gamma(R)$, write $u=n(n^{-1}un)n^{-1}$; both homomorphisms therefore take the value $f_N(n)f_\beta(n^{-1}un)f_N(n)^{-1}$. They agree on all root groups and on $T$. Sheaf generation in [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] gives equality on $G$: locally every point is a product of such points, the values on the product agree, and the sheaf uniqueness axiom identifies their global values. This does not require checking the relation hypotheses on any separately supplied data.
